added_failures_source: The two contract fields are derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs as the node requires and both read clean: baseline_suite base-arm-current.log 5 failed/7 passed EXIT=1 at 50b923338 (the node's own five new tests), after_suite head-arm-current.log 12 passed EXIT=0 at 84d8ac551. But the node's gate is only three files (test_producer_says_why_it_stops, test_producer_holds_a_lease, test_crew_watch_stream) and omits the consumers of the function it changed. An independent wider arm I ran (nine follow/watch test files: test_crew_ticker, test_crew_recovery, test_follow_*, test_follower_*, test_crew_watch_lifetime) gives the same 192 passed at base 50b923338 and 3 failed/189 passed at head 84d8ac551, so the true added-failure set is 3 and is recorded under findings, not here, because these fields are pinned to the reviewed run's own arms.

findings.text: regression: the new unconditional `click.echo(f"reckon crew watch stopped: {stop_reason}", err=True)` in crew_watch's finally runs on every `crew watch --follow` exit, adding a line to the follower's output that it never produced before. Three existing tests regress, all passing at base 50b923338 and failing at head 84d8ac551 in an identical tree: tests/test_crew_ticker.py::test_cli_follow_prints_compact_transition_lines_by_default (output line count 1 -> 2: 'reckon crew watch stopped: watch stream ended' appended), tests/test_crew_ticker.py::test_cli_follow_keeps_machine_objects_behind_json_flag and tests/test_crew_recovery.py::test_cli_follow_streams_each_event_as_one_json_document (JSONDecodeError on the non-JSON stop line). Removing exactly that echo line from the head makes all three pass (EXIT=0), so the line is the cause. The reviewed run's three-file gate does not include these files, so its own arms read clean and the regression went unmeasured.

follow-on: the manifest declares docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/producer-that-stops-says-why.html and a docs/figures/crew-runtime-positive-controls/producer-that-stops-says-why figures directory among its write paths, but neither exists at the reviewed head. The section's first done-when asks the 19:47-19:55Z death's cause be stated with the evidence each claim rests on; as delivered that analysis lives only in the manifest evidence_inputs, so promotion leaves no evidence artifact for that clause.

item_verdicts.diff: read the two commits against base 50b923338: 06d9bfed adds _logged_producer_stop, the FOLLOWER_PRODUCER_STOPPED_EVENT wiring in _follow_watch_lines, and the lease/signal/exception stop-reason writer around the crew_watch loop; 84d8ac551 strips the producer's log timestamp prefix and loosens the renewal test lease interval. Diffstat reckon/cli.py +78/-13, tests/test_producer_says_why_it_stops.py new +168.
item_verdicts.done_when: the code half is test_producer_says_why_it_stops.py (5 tests). I re-ran the head arm at 84d8ac551 to 12 passed EXIT=0, the base arm at 50b923338 to 5 failed/7 passed EXIT=1, and my own mutation removing the stop-reason echo line reddened the lease test EXIT=1 - so the guard does fire. But the node's gate is three files and the function it changed (_follow_watch_lines) is consumed by crew follow/crew watch --follow; a wider arm shows 192 passed at base vs 3 failed/189 passed at head, so the done-when's 'test drives that path' is met while a regression it caused is unmeasured by its own gate.
item_verdicts.goal: the node delivers the guaranteed-delivery half of the section: a watch producer records why it ended (lease expiry, received signal, uncaught exception) and its follower surfaces that final logged reason. _logged_producer_stop reads the tail of the producer service log and crew_watch writes 'reckon crew watch stopped: <reason>' before exit. The same line is written on the follower's own exit and contaminates its output, which the section did not ask for.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits 06d9bfed and 84d8ac551, orientation_base_sha 50b923338, baseline_suite 5 failed/7 passed completed EXIT=1, after_suite 12 passed completed EXIT=0 at 84d8ac551, negative_control-current.log 1 failed EXIT=1, ruff '4 existing findings at base and head; both format checks passed'. Its arms are honest for the three files they cover but too narrow to see the regression.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's declared write paths; the head diff touches exactly reckon/cli.py and tests/test_producer_says_why_it_stops.py, both inside them. The two declared evidence paths (docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/producer-that-stops-says-why.html and the docs/figures/crew-runtime-positive-controls/producer-that-stops-says-why directory) are absent from the tree, so no out-of-scope file is touched but two declared paths are unused.

justifications.durability: the stop-reason line is written from the runner immediately before exit and the follower reports it once, so a producer stopping for a catchable reason leaves a durable cause; the renewal test was widened to tolerate storage contention. Against that, the write is unconditional and reaches a path the section did not scope - the follower's own display - durably breaking crew watch --follow's compact and JSON output contracts in three existing tests; a change that regresses sibling contracts is not durable. A SIGKILL or host/cgroup termination cannot write the line and remains uncovered.
justifications.evidence: the node's own guard is shown to fire - base arm 5 failed/7 passed EXIT=1 at 50b923338, head arm 12 passed EXIT=0 at 84d8ac551, and my independent mutation removing the stop-reproduced stop-reason echo line reddens the lease test EXIT=1. Deduction: the gate is too narrow to measure the change's blast radius - the function it changed is consumed by crew follow, and a wider nine-file arm reads 192 passed at base vs 3 failed/189 passed at head, all three added failures attributable to the same echo line (removing it passes all three). A strict measure asks that the recorded evidence cover the changed path's consumers, which this one does not.
justifications.fit: the change adds one event constant beside the existing reload event pair and reuses runs.watch_log_path, runs.producer_live, runs.watch_lease_renewed_at and runs.producer_my_lease_seconds rather than re-deriving lease logic; tests follow the node-test idiom (real subprocess for the lease case, CliRunner for signal/exception). But the same echo breaks the established compact-line and JSON-line output contracts two sibling suites assert, so it fits the new behaviour at the cost of existing ones.
justifications.goal_fidelity: crew_watch composes a stop reason on three paths (un-renewed lease, SIGTERM/SIGHUP, caught exception) and echoes it to the service log; _logged_producer_stop reads that final line and _follow_watch_lines emits FOLLOWER_PRODUCER_STOPPED_EVENT so the follower reports it, which is the section's headline requirement. Deductions: the echo is emitted on the follower's own exit path as well, regressing three existing tests the section did not intend to touch; and the section's first done-when, that the historical death's cause be landed with its evidence, survives only in the manifest evidence_inputs with no evidence artifact.
justifications.scope_discipline: the head diff touches exactly two files, reckon/cli.py (+78/-13) and tests/test_producer_says_why_it_stops.py (new +168), both within the declared write paths; no plan, sprint or server file is modified, ruff finds no new finding, and no AI or plan identifier appears in the code or commit bodies. Deduction: file discipline is clean, but the declared gate scoped to three unrelated files while the changed function's consumers were untested, so the verification scope, not the write scope, is where the miss is.
